about: Data2Peak's talk-owned data (bake/remap.py), from the kit bake's toys.json, falling-big.f32, d0.f32 and d0-significance.json.

falling.about: toys.json's falling toy (simulated, seed 1540) redrawn on the series' mass axis by talks/2026_00_00_Data2Peak/bake/remap.py: m' = 1816 + (m - 1.45) x 320 MeV/c2 per GeV, 30 bins of 3.2 MeV/c2 on 1 816-1 912 MeV/c2. Counts, z, alarms and rolls are the bake's own; only x values move. A falling spectrum (simulated): density proportional to exp(slope (m - lo)/(hi - lo)) on lo-hi GeV, 30 bins of 10 MeV, 140 entries a roll, 20 rolls drawn one after another from one generator. z is the one-sided Poisson significance of each bin against its expected count (p = P(N >= n | expected), z = Phi^-1(1-p)); an alarm fires where z >= 2. The roll with the largest z is then grown to 3 500 entries by adding 3 360 more from the same generator.

curve.about: the toy's expectation as dk-curve 'exp' sets on the MeV axis (slope per MeV/c2, pivot 1816, bin 3.2): the same a, the same curve per bin as the bake's GeV sets

first186About: rows 1-186 of record 401 in file order that fall in 1820-1840, 1850-1880 or 1890-1910 MeV/c2 (139 rows), counted in 10 MeV/c2 bins from 1 820: window 79 = staysAbove5From.on, side bands 60 = staysAbove5From.off. A dk-hist reads it with src 't2.json', key 'first186', lo 1820, bin 10.
